title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-03-01
source: Ampex MM-1000 16 Track Master Two Inch Wide Tape- Multi Track Mix-down To DAT By Dan Healy @ 44.1KHz); DAT x ONE by Dick Latvala- DAT x TWO(Mine); Editing(Adobe Audition CC)-FLAC encoding(dBpoweramp)-Tagging(Tag & Re-name) Jim Wise; This is a 100% Flat transfer from the DAT no signal processing what-so-ever. Some Pitch Correction Implemented

ai_review.summary: Flat‑transfer soundboard capture of a 1969 show that shines on Dupree's Diamond, The Eleven and Other One, with crystal‑clear mix despite a weak Hey Jude.
ai_review.review: The multi‑track SBD flat transfer is praised as crisp, clean and almost studio‑like, letting the band’s 1969 fire shine through.  Highlights include an acoustic‑driven Dupree's Diamond Blues, a soaring The Eleven, a powerful Other One and a lovely Lovelight, while the infamous Hey Jude falls flat.  A few reviewers note minor pitch‑correction quirks and occasional patchiness, but overall the performance is regarded as dynamite.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both the recording (flat‑transfer, crystal clear) and the musical performance (multiple standout jams). Minor criticisms are limited to a few songs and pitch‑correction notes, so the weighted average lands in the upper‑mid range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Flat transfer praised as the cleanest possible copy; crisp separation of instruments and vocal detail. Some reviewers mention speed/pitch wobble corrections needed on certain tracks, but overall no dropout or muffiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set opens strong with acoustic Dupree's and Mountains, leading into a tight The Eleven in the second set.  The band maintains high energy throughout, though occasional tempo/pitch quirks are noted; overall the show is viewed as a solid, classic ’69 performance.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly highlighted for his soaring guitar tone, acoustic work on Dupree's and Mountains, and dominant presence that drives the jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for an inspiring solo during The Eleven and strong interplay with Jerry; praised for “inspired licks” in the second set.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned for blazing trails in the first half of The Eleven and taking a shortcut through its outro, leading into Lovelight.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ at 15:05 (Dark Star) called ‘prime time’; overall keyboard texture praised throughout the show.
